questions.question: 1. What is the main characteristic of a point operation in image processing?

answers.a: The output pixel value depends only on the corresponding input pixel value
answers.b: The output pixel value depends only on neighbouring pixels
answers.c: The image must first be converted into a binary image
answers.d: The operation can be applied only to colour images

explanations.a: Correct. In a point operation, the output pixel value is obtained by applying a transformation to the corresponding input pixel value.
explanations.b: Incorrect. This describes a neighbourhood-based operation, where surrounding pixels contribute to the output.
explanations.c: Incorrect. A point operation does not require the input image to be converted into a binary image.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Point operations can be applied to grayscale images, including the grayscale images considered in this experiment.

questions.question: 2. For an 8-bit grayscale image, what is the usual valid range of a pixel value $p$?

explanations.a: Incorrect. This range excludes one endpoint of the grayscale range and includes a value outside the usual 8-bit range.
explanations.b: Correct. An 8-bit grayscale image normally represents pixel values from $0$ to $255$.
explanations.c: Incorrect. The value $256$ is outside the usual valid range for an 8-bit grayscale pixel.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Negative pixel values are not part of the usual valid grayscale range for an 8-bit image.

questions.question: 3. In the linear point transformation $q = sp + o$, which parameter determines the slope of the transformation?

explanations.a: Incorrect. In the linear transformation, this parameter represents the offset rather than the slope.
explanations.b: Incorrect. This symbol represents the output pixel value produced by the transformation.
explanations.c: Correct. In $q = sp + o$, $s$ is the slope of the transformation and controls how the input gray levels are stretched or compressed.
explanations.d: Incorrect. This symbol represents the input pixel value to which the transformation is applied.

questions.question: 4. A linear point transformation is given by $q = 4p + 160$. For an input pixel with $p = 20$, what is the transformed value before any range adjustment?

explanations.a: Incorrect. This value does not result from substituting $p = 20$ into the given transformation.
explanations.b: Incorrect. This value does not include the full contribution of the slope term in the given transformation.
explanations.c: Incorrect. This value does not result from substituting $p = 20$ into the given transformation.

questions.question: 5. Which transformation is particularly useful for expanding a narrow range of low-intensity values while compressing higher-intensity values?

explanations.a: Correct. A logarithmic transformation such as $q = c \log(1+p)$ expands a narrow range of low-intensity values while compressing higher-intensity values.
explanations.b: Incorrect. A window function is used to preserve a selected range of input gray levels rather than to provide the logarithmic mapping described here.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Clipping uses a piece-wise linear mapping with specified input limits.
explanations.d: Incorrect. A constant-value transformation does not provide the nonlinear intensity mapping described in this experiment.

questions.question: 6. In the clipping transformation, what happens to an input pixel value $p$ that is greater than the upper limit $b$?

answers.b: It is mapped to $255$ for the 8-bit grayscale case
answers.d: It is left unchanged in every case

explanations.a: Incorrect. The lower output value is associated with input values below the lower limit in the clipping function.
explanations.b: Correct. For the 8-bit grayscale case described in the experiment, an input value above $b$ is mapped to the upper output value $255$.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Multiplication by the slope applies to the linear part of the piece-wise transformation within the specified input interval.
explanations.d: Incorrect. The clipping function changes input values that fall outside the specified interval.

questions.question: 7. Consider a window function that preserves the input range $a \leq p \leq b$ and maps values outside this range to $0$. What is the main purpose of this operation?

answers.a: To preserve all gray levels without modification
answers.b: To make every pixel equal to $255$
answers.c: To select a desired range of gray levels for the output
answers.d: To make the output depend on neighbouring pixels

explanations.a: Incorrect. A window function specifically suppresses input values outside the selected range.
explanations.b: Incorrect. A window function does not map every pixel to the maximum grayscale value.
explanations.c: Correct. The window function preserves a selected range of gray levels and suppresses values outside that range.
explanations.d: Incorrect. A window function is a point operation, so the output is determined from the corresponding input pixel rather than its neighbours.

questions.question: 8. Two point transformations are applied to the same input image. Transformation A is linear, while Transformation B is logarithmic. Which statement best describes their difference?

answers.a: Both transformations must produce identical output values
answers.b: Transformation A uses neighbouring pixels, while Transformation B uses one pixel
answers.c: Transformation A can only decrease pixel values, while Transformation B can only increase them
answers.d: The relationship between input and output pixel values is linear for A and nonlinear for B

explanations.a: Incorrect. Different transformation functions can map the same input pixel values to different output values.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Both transformations described here are point operations and use the corresponding input pixel value.
explanations.c: Incorrect. The effect of a transformation depends on its parameters and the input values; these restrictions do not characterize the two transformations.
explanations.d: Correct. A linear transformation has a linear relationship between $p$ and $q$, whereas the logarithmic transformation has a nonlinear relationship.

questions.question: 9. Suppose a point operation produces an output value $q$ outside the valid range $0 \leq q \leq 255$. What is required before the value can be represented as a valid 8-bit grayscale pixel?

answers.a: The value must be adjusted or mapped so that it lies within the valid grayscale range
answers.b: The value must always be replaced by the input pixel value
answers.c: The value must always be converted into a negative number
answers.d: The value must be made dependent on neighbouring pixels

explanations.a: Correct. The transformed value must be brought into the valid 8-bit grayscale range before it can be represented as an 8-bit pixel.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Replacing the result with the original input value would discard the effect of the selected point transformation.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Negative values are outside the valid range for an 8-bit grayscale pixel.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Introducing neighbouring pixels would change the operation from a point operation to a neighbourhood-based operation.
